market: Prices are Wednesday 25-Nov closes for all four markets. DIB rose 1.6% to 8.92 on ~3x average volume. Oil rebounded: Brent's February contract settled $90.91 (+2.4%), its first close above $90 since 17-Nov (other reports quote the expiring front month near $94.6), WTI $84.15, on the Ras Tanura claim, three vessels struck near Hormuz (UKMTO) and pre-holiday short covering, despite a 1.1m bbl US crude build; OPEC+ meets 29-Nov with Iraq and Kazakhstan pushing for higher capacity baselines (Investing.com; Nation Thailand). US: October PCE +0.3% m/m headline and core; core 3.3% y/y vs 3.2% expected, the highest since November 2023; Q3 GDP revised up to 4.3% from 3.4%; futures price a 25 bp hike on 9-Dec and another in January; S&P 500 -0.3% after an intraday drop of 3.2% (Kotak Neo citing BEA). US markets are shut today for Thanksgiving. No new Tadawul foreign-flow print since the week to 5-Nov.

title: DIB back to index weight, the money moves to ADIB
brief:
The fund beat the index by 6.9 bps today, taking us to +74 bps since launch, as TASI slipped 0.6% on the Houthi claim of a strike at Ras Tanura while the UAE kept rising on its own story.

DIB's board approved buying Emirates Islamic with 3.49bn new shares, which leaves Emirates NBD with 32.5% of the bank but gives no valuation or EPS figures, and since DIB brings about 73% of the combined assets while its holders keep only 67.5% of the shares, I took the overweight off at AED 8.92 and moved the money into ADIB.

My view is that the deal may still be good, but the stock already prices a good outcome, so the main risk is paying up before the General Assembly circular shows the numbers.

analysis: Benchmark +0.007%, fund +0.064%. Attribution: allocation +5.8 bps (Saudi underweight +3.7 as the Saudi slice fell 0.42%; Qatar overweight +1.9) and selection -6.1 bps (Saudi -9.7: our Saudi names -0.64% vs -0.42%; UAE +4.6: ours +0.66% vs +0.52% over Friday-Monday; Qatar -1.7; Kuwait +0.7). What we did and why: (1) Pending switch booked as ordered before Monday's session: sold 134,000 ADNOC L&S at 7.37 and bought 115,100 DIB at 8.56. DIB's 11% jump came during the session, after the order, so the fill is honest, but it means we now own an acquisition story rather than the cheap, low-beta bank we chose: the stock is RSI 82 and 13% above its 200-day, and Q3 profit fell 3% on impairments. We keep it to the board outcome on 25-Nov and set a clear rule (cut to index weight if the deal is paid in new DIB shares on dilutive terms, or if talks fail and the price falls back below 7.9). (2) Oil rules fired on a settle, as planned: Brent $89.37 is below the $90 level for ADNOC Drilling (cut to index weight, ~0.66%) and Luberef (to index weight, ~0.23%). The driver is supply (Libya, IEA ~2m b/d Q4 surplus, Gulf exports near pre-war), exactly the scenario the rule was built for; Aramco is already at index weight. (3) Jarir. This is guidance, not noise: a ~11% permanent cut to the earnings base from 2027, and the stock broke its 200-day on 2.7x normal volume. The price fall (8%) roughly matches the earnings cut, so it is no cheaper on 2027 numbers; its quality (ROE still ~60% after the tax) and ~6% yield remain, and the dividend and ROE rules are not breached, so we halve the overweight (+1.5 to ~+0.75 pts) rather than exit. Lesson: our largest Saudi overweight carried a disclosed tax risk (flagged in its 2024-25 statements) that our factor model does not see; the quarterly review will screen the Saudi overweights for DMTT exposure (multinational groups above EUR 750m revenue with low effective tax). (4) Reinvestment. The Luberef and Jarir sales would take Saudi to ~-9.9 pts against the 10-pt limit, so we took Al Rajhi, our largest Saudi stock-level underweight, to index weight; that is risk control, not a call that Saudi has turned (TASI is 3% below its 50-day, 178 decliners, no flow data). title: Oil breaks $90, so the oil bets come off
brief:
The fund gained 5.7 bps on the day, most of it from a missed STC dividend we booked late, while DIB's 11% jump cancelled out Jarir's 8% fall on the new Saudi minimum tax.

Brent settled at $89.37, its first close below $90, which was the rule for ADNOC Drilling and Luberef, so both went back to index weight, and I halved the Jarir overweight because the tax takes about 11% off its profit from 2027.

My view is that the fund now relies less on oil and more on domestic earnings, and the main risk is a supply shock that sends Brent back up just after we sold.

title: Missile hits an Aramco building in Riyadh
brief:

My view is that conflict risk is concentrated in Saudi Arabia more than anywhere else in the Gulf, and the risk is that we stay underweight too long once that changes.

title: Tawuniya jumps, Emaar's buyout is cash

title: Oil falls 8.6%, Aramco cut to index weight
brief:
Brent fell 8.6% after the US midterms, taking it below our $95 line for Aramco, so I cut Aramco to index weight and moved the money into Al Rajhi, Alinma and Ma'aden to stay inside the Saudi limit.

The fund lagged by 6.2 bps as risk-on buying lifted the higher-beta Saudi names we hold less of, while the IHC underweight paid again, and AD Ports was trimmed for liquidity.

My view is that this was risk control rather than a call that the Saudi sell-off is over, and the risk is a sharp rebound we are not set up for.

title: e& trimmed on one-offs, KFH added
brief:
The fund slipped 0.8 bps as UAE telecoms eased, and I trimmed e& after finding that most of its 46% profit growth came from a one-off Vodafone gain, which puts the real P/E near 14.7x, not 9x.

With Aramco's results and the US midterms out of the way, I put spare cash into KFH, the lowest-beta large bank in the Gulf, with profit up 6.2% and costs falling.

My view is that clean earnings matter more than headline growth, and the risk with KFH is any Iranian strike on Kuwait.

title: Oil drops on diplomacy, NMDC trimmed

title: Day one: Qatar rallies, Elm trimmed

headline: Fund launched: 48 positions, Saudi underweight, defensives and energy-logistics overweight
market: Brent settled near $115 (up ~14% in October) as Houthi strikes on Saudi energy sites and tanker incidents near Hormuz pushed risk premia higher; TASI fell 2.7% on 25-Oct, its worst day since April 2025, while Qatar held flat. US midterms on 3-Nov and the risk of US action on Iran are the next catalysts.
positioning: Saudi -8.2% vs index (moved into Qatar +2.9%, UAE +2.6%, Kuwait +0.7%). Largest single bet: IHC -4.6% (22x P/E, no dividend, weak trend). Largest overweights: Aramco, STC, Jarir, Zain, ADNOC L&S, NMDC, e&, du.
analysis: Every name in the 99-stock index plus 28 off-index candidates was scored on value (earnings yield, dividend yield, price-to-book), quality (ROE, EPS growth, leverage), momentum (6-month return, distance from 200-day average, 1-month return) and low beta, then adjusted for the current regime: favour beneficiaries of high oil and shipping disruption and low-beta defensives; avoid airlines, Saudi travel/hospitality and refiners in the strike zone. The fund is cheaper (12.5x vs 13.8x), higher-yielding (4.1% vs 3.5%), higher-ROE (24% vs 21%) and lower-beta (0.72 vs 0.80) than the benchmark.
trades: Initial purchase of 48 positions; KWD ~200k held in cash (2%).
watch: US midterms (3-Nov) and any US-Iran escalation; damage reports on Aramco sites; Q3 results still due from smaller Saudi/UAE names; Shariah board sign-off on the 7 off-index names.
title: The fund is launched
brief:
We launched a 10m KWD paper fund with 48 stocks against the S&P GCC All Share Islamic index, with Saudi Arabia underweight because it carries the most conflict risk and Qatar, the UAE and Kuwait overweight.

The biggest single bet is not owning much IHC, which trades at 22x earnings with no dividend, and the fund is cheaper, higher yielding and lower beta than the index.

My view is that this is a portfolio built for a nervous Gulf, and the main risk is a fast peace that rewards everything we chose to own less of.
